children: India's consumer inflation likely accelerated to 4.9% on year in August from 4.45% in July, according to the median estimate of five economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. That would mark the highest reading this year and since the government revamped its consumer-price index data series in January. Vegetable prices continued to rise alongside a sharp jump in sugar prices, while higher gold prices likely pressured the core inflation, HSBC economists say in a note. Volatile energy prices have also raised input cost pressures that could gradually pass through to consumers, even as retail fuel prices have been kept unchanged since May, says DBS Group Research. The data is expected to be released on Monday. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
